title: Benbow's show goes to Havana after the storm
summary: Moore's third departure from Birmingham led to Benbow's show in Havana's Tropical Gardens just after a destructive storm.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Freddie Moore (Ron Welburn) (April 5, 1983):
This particular show you're speaking of, I was with William Benbow.
William Benbow.
William Benbow's show. I joined him one of the... The third time I left Birmingham, I joined him, William Benbow, I think in (?) or Detroit, to South Carolina, North Carolina...
We went down to Havana, Cuba. I played this big theatre there. I think it was named Tropical Theatre. The theatre held round about five thousand people.
What was the name of it again?
Tropical Gardens.
Tropical Gardens.
Yeah. And we stayed there, with a nice little (?) band there. Right after the War, I think after the First World War, the Second...?
Well, it must have been after the First World War.
Yeah. All them big, nice churches and buildings were just torn down. They squooshed 'em all to pieces.
Why were they...?
They had a big tropical storm.
Oh, they had storms. I see.
Moore (II) - 2
A storm there that... And a lot of bombing(?). You know, they had that big...
People were out on the street. They were...
Well, they tore the whole building down! A big wall!
I see. And these were the cathedrals and some of the public houses.
Yeah. These nice churches. Everything just was blown. Tore 'em all to pieces. Bombed down.
Bombed down.

We went over there right after that. I think we stayed over there about three months. Different places. Not the same place all the time. We still had... We always carried about six pieces, a five- or six-piece band with us.
But it was the same kind of act that was performing in the States.
Yeah, same kind of acts. I think it had about six chorus girls, and a soubrette, and a singer, a dancer and a comedian.
